pr_title: Avoid div by zero by preventing returning a grid bounds with zero width or height (take 2)
pr_body:
Fix #4146 

This time the issue was that the Sprite::DefaultGridBounds was being set to a rect with width or height equals to zero. So the following measures were taken:
1. Do not allow the user to enter values lesser than 1 into the width and height widgets on the grid's preferences configuration section.
2. Add some checks to force setting width or height to 1 when the caller is trying to set a grid bounds with width or height lesser to 1.

comments: It looks like this bug isn't fixed. We've received crash reports about it in v1.3.7: https://igara-studio.sentry.io/share/issue/bd557a54cd9b4c44a72e83ef868ed231/

Been looking at this, and seems that the only way that it could happen is by setting a default grid size having w=0 and h=0 in the preferences dialog.
So, we can do one of the following:
1. Modify void Sprite::SetDefaultGridBounds(const gfx::Rect& defGridBounds) to detect when the caller is trying to set an empty defGridBounds and then set the width and/or height of the default grid bounds equals to 1.
2. Just avoid executing the offending line by surrounding it with an if clause that checks if the grid bounds are not empty.
3. Do not allow to enter zero for width and height in the grid preferences.

Which one do you think is better? I think I would go for 1 to prevent, and 3 for a better UX.

We have to avoid storing a grid with width/height = 0. If the user enters 0 in width and height, the grid should end with a grid of 1x1. The same for scripts or if an invalid grid is stored in .aseprite files, etc.
Just in case, we must do this in the most low level function, e.g. `doc::Sprite::setGridBounds` // and add asserts, if() etc to avoid the div by zero, just in case.
